FOREWORD

0.1 This. Indian Standard ( Part II ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 31 October 1969, after the draft finalized by the Methods of Chemical Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council. 0.2 In IS : 2927-i964*, 24 grades of silver-copper brazing alloys have been In order to determine correctly the composition of different specified. silver-copper brazing alloys, methods of analysis have been described in various parts of this standard. Determination of silver and copper as prescribed for silver-copper brazing alloys except BA-CuAg7 and BACuAg8 is covered in IS : 4667 ( Part I )-1968. This standard ( Part II ) describes the methods for silver, copper and tin in BA-CuAg7 and BA-CuAg8. Methods for analysis of zinc, cadmium and nickel will be covered in subsequent parts. 0.3 In the formulation of this standard, due weightage has been given to international coTordination among the standards and practices prevailing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in the field in this country. This has been met by deriving assistance from the ` 1967 Rook of ASTM methods for chemical analysis of metals: Part 32 ' issued by the American Society for Testing and Materials. 0.4 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the-final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : Z-19607.

5. DETERMINATION
METHOD

GRAVIMETRIC

5.1 Outline of Method - After separation of tin from the solution of the sample, silver is precipitated as silver chloride by means of hydrochloric The precipitate is filtered, washed, dried and weighed. acid.

5.3 Procedure 5.3.1 Take a suitable aliquot from the solution preserved under 4.3.3 and boil. Add suficient amount of dilute hydrochloric acid slowly lvith constant stirring till the precipitation is complete. Add a few ml of dilute hydrochloric acid in excess. Let it stand for about an hour, keeping it warm.

5.3.2 Decant the solution through a weighed sintered glass crucible. \\rash the precipitate twice with warm dilute nitric acid and decant Transfer the precipitate to the crucible and wash through the crucible. Transfer the filtrate and the with hot water till free fl-om chloride. washings to a XHJ-ml beaker and reserve for the determination of copper (see 6.4.1 ). 5.3.3 hours. IS : 4667 ( Part 11) - 1969 6. DETERMINATION METHOD OF COPPER BY THE ELECTROLYTIC

6.1 Outline of Method - After the separation of tin and silver from the solution of the sample, copper is deposited electrolytically from the solution and weighed. 6.2 Apparatus - The following platinum electrodes (see Fig. 1 ) are recommended but strict adherence to the shape and size of the electrodes In order to decrease the time of the deposition, one of is not essential. the types of rotating forms of electrodes generally available for agitation of the electrolyte may be employed.

1 50

-!L Io-30@ -AL 400 MESH/cm'
IA Cylindrical Platinum Cathode IB Spiral Platinum Anode All dimensions in millimetres.

FIG. 1

CYLINDRICAL'PLAT~NUM CATHODE

AND

SPIRAL

PLATINUM ANODE

6.2.1 (;&ode - It may be formed either from plain or perforated sheet or from wire gauze. 6.2.1.1 Gauge cathodes made preferably from gauze containing 400-mesh/cm2 should be used. The wire used for making gauze should be approsimately 0.20 mm in diameter. Cathodes should be stiffened by doubling the gauze for about 3 mm on the top and bottom or by reinfnrcing the gauze at the top and bottom or with a platinum ring or band. 6.2.1.2 The diameter and height of the cylinder should be approximately 30 mm and 50 mm respectively. The stem should be made from platinum alloy wire, such as platinum-iridium, platinum-rhodium or platinum-ruthenium having diameter of approximately l-5 mm. It should 6 .

IS : 4667 ( Part II ) - 1969

be flattened and welded to the entire height of the gauze. height of the cathode including the stem should approximately

The overall be 130 mm.

6.2.2 Anode - Either a spiral or a gauze anode should be used. The spiral anode should be made from l-0 mm or larger platinum wire formed into a spiral of seven coils with a height of approximately 50 mm and diameter of 12 mm, the overall height including the stem being 130 mm. The gauze anode should be made of the same material and of the same general design as platinum gauze cathode specified under 6.2.1. 6.3 Reageuts

6.4 Procedure
6.4.1 To the filtrate aud washings reserved under 5.3.2, add 5 ml of concentrated sulphuric acid and evaporate to fumes, cool, dilute to 200 ml and add 5 ml of concentrated nitric acid. Add 2 g of urea, insert the electrodes, the cathode having been accurately weighed; cover wilh a pair of split cover-glass and electrolyze for 16 hours at a current density of 0% A/dm* ( at this current density, the electrolysis is conveniently carried on overnight ), or at a current density of 4 A/dm" for a short period ( about 2 hours ). In the latter case, one of the types of rotating forms of elcctrodes generally available may be used. When the solution becomes colourless reduce the current density to 0.3 A/dm2 and continue electrolysis until the deposition of copper is complete as indicated by the absence of plating on the new surface of the electrode obtained by lowering the electrode.

6.4.2 Without interrupting the current, lower the beaker slowly while washing thoroughly with water and collecting the washings into the electrolyte, Remove the cathode quickly while washing further with water; rinse it with water in a beaker and then dip it in two successive Dry the cathode in an air oven at 100�C baths of ethanol or methanol. for three to five minutes, cool and weigh for copper. 6.5 Calculation Copper, where
